item.title: Cailar & Carla
item.description:
Product Overview

In Taiwan, there is a growing emphasis on art education, yet a significant gap in students’ understanding and exploration of color concepts. Cailar & Carla aimed to bridge this gap by creating an interactive learning product to introduce elementary students to the fundamentals of color theory.

Cailar & Carla is an interactive color learning product designed for elementary students (ages 7–11) to explore color theory through hands-on play. By integrating a plush tactile controller and an accompanying physical picture book with a gamified mobile app, children can capture colors from their real-world environment to solve challenges. This multimodal approach addresses the lack of engaging, depth-oriented color education in current curriculums.

item.title: Chami
item.description:
Product Overview

Chami is an interactive chameleon robot designed specifically for pediatric waiting rooms. It features a fun color-matching game and provides responsive and engaging interaction to help young patients adjust to the often-frightening hospital environment.

Key features of Chami include:

  • Tactile Comfort: The prototype is crafted with a soft green fabric exterior, making it comforting and inviting for children to touch.
  • Emotional Support: Chami uses non-verbal communication to interact with children. It changes its LED eye patterns and makes simple sounds depending on what the child says or does.
  • Playful Interaction: Children play the game by pressing the physical buttons on Chami’s body to match the colors displayed on its eyes.

item.title: Ocean
item.description:
Product Overviews

In modern society, phone notifications frequently disrupt our concentration and can even affect our emotional well-being. This constant stream of alerts not only diverts our attention but also results in decreased productivity. Conversely, missing important messages often leads to feelings of anxiety. Therefore, it is essential to find an effective way to achieve balance.

Ocean is an interactive device that helps users reduce anxiety caused by notification interruptions, enabling a more focused and mindful experience while they can receive important messages.

item.title: Slime Strategy
item.description:
Product Overview

Many strategy games on the market either require significant time investment or are overly simplistic. As a result, people with limited time often choose other game genres for relaxation, leading them to avoid strategy games altogether.

Slime Strategy is a strategy game that combines a compelling storyline with easy accessibility, allowing players to learn the game mechanics in just 5 minutes and complete it within a total playtime of 30 minutes.

item.title: The Entity
item.description:
Project Overview

The core goal of this project was to design an experience that makes users feel genuinely uncomfortable and weird. We shaped this atmosphere by centering the interaction around an idol that constantly “watches” the participant while they solving the puzzle.

Instead of giving clear written instructions, we used light and sound cues to guide participants to complete the process step by step. The interaction builds up to a climax where they are forced to physically squeeze a tangible heart. By mixing the creepy feeling of being observed with the actual physical resistance of squeezing the heart, we wanted to turn a simple installation into an intense, ritualistic experience.

item.title: Wearable Risk Awareness System
item.description:
Project Overview

This is an Ergonomic Risk Awareness System designed to detect whether workers are using dangerous postures during lifting. It is an edge-computing wearable device that provides real-time posture detection and delivers delayed vibration feedback, gently alerting workers to hazardous postures only when necessary, effectively preventing injuries while minimizing workflow disruption.

The Problem & Motivation

Occupational musculoskeletal disorders (MSDs), particularly low back pain, are a major global health challenge. In the European context, work-related MSDs account for over 40% of all work-related health problems and are a primary cause of sick leave and early retirement among manual workers.
